Sweyn Holm.narrative: I was born in Brackenford and learned the water before I learned my letters. Most mornings I'm out on the river or up the north shore before the gate opens, and I sell what I catch in the square and pay the Guild its stall rent. I keep to my boat and my house; Beorn is about the only man I talk to freely. The gate-due and the town's quarrels are not my business — the fish don't care who is Reeve.
values: a quiet day on the water
an honest catch sold at a fair price
goals: keep the stall rent paid to the Market Guild
catch enough to salt and smoke for winter
teach Knut to swim and handle a line

relations.name: Astrid Holm
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She smokes and sells what I bring in; we work well together without needing many words.

relations.name: Knut Holm
relations.label: son
relations.note: He's always by the water; I'll have him in the boat soon enough.

relations.name: Beorn Beornson
relations.label: friend
relations.note: The one man I'll share a drink with — he knows the woods, I know the river.

relations.name: Mercy Abbot
relations.label: landlord
relations.note: The Guild holds my stall rent; she's fair enough but it's a cost every week.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: reeve
relations.note: He keeps the gate-due off my back since I sell inside the walls, but I don't look to him for anything.

relations.name: Baldwin Wade
relations.label: customer
relations.note: The inn buys fish when it can; his coin is good.

relations.name: Sigrun Beornson
relations.label: stall neighbour
relations.note: She sells her man's venison beside my fish; a sharp trader, but honest at the stall.

memories.gist: The Lean Year came and the river still gave fish, so we ate while the fields failed.
Beorn pulled me out of the shallows when a snag took my leg and the current turned; I owe him a debt I can't put marks to.
The morning Astrid said she was carrying Knut, I came in off the water early and we sat by the fire all day.
The first time I took Knut down to the bank and he laughed at the water, I knew he'd be a river child.
A winter squall caught me off the north shore and I rowed home with the boat half full; I've watched the sky closer since.

stances.why: The Guild can put me off the square, and the square is how the catch becomes marks.
The Reeve and the Guild can fight; my boat doesn't take sides.
When the fields failed in the Lean Year the water still gave, and I trust it more than any ledger.
Beorn pulled me out once; I'd do the same for him and he knows it.
A full smokehouse is a quiet winter, and quiet winters are what I want.

Astrid Holm.narrative: I keep the house by the river and the smokehouse behind it, and I sell our fish at the Guild stall in the square. Sweyn brings the catch in and I make it worth marks — smoked, salted, laid out clean. I worry about the stall rent and about the winters, but I don't say so much. Knut is never far from the water and I've stopped trying to keep him from it.
goals: keep the smokehouse full enough to sell through winter
clear the stall rent each week without borrowing
see Knut grow up strong and river-wise

relations.name: Sweyn Holm
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He brings it in and I make it sell; we don't need to talk much to work together.

relations.name: Knut Holm
relations.label: son
relations.note: Always at the water's edge — I watch him and let him be.

relations.name: Mercy Abbot
relations.label: guild head
relations.note: She sets the stall terms; I pay them and keep my peace.

relations.name: Sigrun Beornson
relations.label: stall neighbour
relations.note: We mind each other's stalls when one of us steps away; she's a good trader.

relations.name: Petra Wade
relations.label: customer
relations.note: The inn's kitchen buys smoked fish from me when the pies need filling.

relations.name: Aethelred Tanner
relations.label: hard bargainer
relations.note: He'll haggle a fish down to nothing if you let him; I don't let him.

relations.name: Sister Alys
relations.label: chapel sister
relations.note: She gave me a salve for Knut's cough last winter and asked nothing.

memories.gist: The Lean Year: the fields failed but Sweyn's catch held, and we sold smoked fish to people who had nothing else.
The day I took the stall in the square for the first time, I sold out before noon and walked home proud.
Knut's first winter he coughed half the season and I hardly slept; Sister Alys's salve and the fire got him through.
The night Sweyn came home half-swamped from the squall, I stood at the door with the lamp till I saw the boat.

stances.why: The Lean Year taught me that what's dried and salted can't be taken by blight or bad weather.
The stall is our living; arguing with the Guild over terms would cost us more than it saves.
He'll live by the river all his life; better he learns it early with us watching.
Debt is how a household loses what it has — I've seen it happen to better-off folk than us.

Knut Holm.narrative: The water is loud and cold and I like it. I sit on the bank and watch the little fish dart and the big boat come in. Mother smells of smoke and father's hands are wet and rough. I want to touch the boat but they say not yet.
goals: catch a fish with my hands

relations.name: Sweyn Holm
relations.label: father
relations.note: He comes home wet and lifts me up high.

relations.name: Astrid Holm
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She smells of smoke and holds me when the water is too loud.

memories.gist: Father lifted me into the boat for a moment and it rocked and I laughed.
I fell in the shallows once and mother pulled me out and wrapped me by the fire.
